analyst_view.overall: Leaders PSV (29 points from 13) host Go Ahead Eagles (9th, 17 points) four days after a 5-1 defeat at Real Madrid in the Champions League, where they led through an Ivan Perisic penalty before collapsing after the break; Peter Bosz called it 'a bad half'. In the league PSV have won their last three by four goals or more (7-0, 6-2, 4-1), and they are without Mauro Junior, Schouten, Plea, Ouaissa and Nagalo, all in the numbers. One injury list rates Perisic a 25% doubt after he left the pitch in Madrid, but Sports Mole's preview lists him in the expected XI and no club news confirms a problem, so I give it little weight. Go Ahead have scored once in their last three league games after 2.3 a game before that, miss Saathof and Marsman, and have Dean James and Linthorst (and, per one list, Margaret) as doubts; Tengstedt is their main threat. Dennis Higler's low card record is already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 4.3 goals, 3.1 for PSV, already trimmed for Mauro Junior and Plea and for Go Ahead's quieter attack lately. I trim slightly to about 4.2 for the Tuesday trip to Madrid, which the numbers have no congestion adjustment for; I have dropped most of my earlier Perisic worry because only one injury list has him as a doubt and Sports Mole expects him to start.

corners.text: The numbers say 11.1 corners, about 7 for PSV as they pin opponents back. Go Ahead may be without wide players Dean James and Margaret and are weaker away, which fits the deep approach the numbers already expect, so I stay at about 11.1.

cards.text: The numbers say 2.4 cards, already lowered about 12% for Dennis Higler, who shows 2.1 cards a game. PSV rarely need to foul at home and Go Ahead's bookings are close to normal, and nothing points to a heated game, so I stay at about 2.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 34.2 shots, 24.6 for PSV. I trim slightly to about 33.2: PSV come off a draining night at the Bernabeu four days earlier, which the numbers do not count, though their league lead and home form keep Bosz from resting many, so it stays a mild lean.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.9 shots on target, 8.0 for PSV. The same Madrid fatigue points slightly lower, to about 11.7; Go Ahead's own attack has gone quiet (one goal in three) but leans on Tengstedt, and the numbers already count their recent shooting.
